1	# Measured observations of the supplied references
2	
3	Measured 2026-09-14 with the bundled asset check and direct pixel reads, then inspected
4	visually at native scale and at 12x nearest-neighbour enlargement
5	(`work/reference-views/`). Measurements are mechanical; the style judgements below are
6	labelled where they are inference rather than measurement.
7	
8	## Identity
9	
10	| | reference.png | reference-b.png |
11	|---|---|---|
12	| sha256 | d997cade…70aa7 | e76b40ce…14a12a |
13	| canvas | 32 x 32 | 32 x 32 |
14	| visible pixels | 390 | 390 |
15	| visible bbox | x 7..24, y 3..27 (18 x 25) | identical |
16	| visible colours | 3 | 2 |
17	| fractional-alpha pixels | 0 | 0 |
18	| opaque components (4-connectivity) | 1 | 1 |
19	
20	## Shared, measured
21	
22	- Identical alpha mask. Every visible pixel in one is visible in the other.
23	- Binary alpha in both files: zero fractional-alpha pixels.
24	- Body colour `#56B5BC` (teal) and detail colour `#F4DDA2` (cream) in both.
25	- Two cream clusters, each exactly 3 wide x 4 tall: x 11..13 and x 18..20, both y 14..17.
26	  They read as eyes and are mirror-symmetric about the figure's vertical axis.
27	- The figure is bilaterally symmetric and front-facing, with two vertical stalks at the
28	  top separated by a notch.
29	- No anti-aliasing and no dithering in either file.
30	
31	## The outline disagreement, measured
32	
33	The two files differ in exactly 180 pixels, and every one of those differences is the
34	same substitution: `#25354A` (dark navy) in reference.png becomes `#56B5BC` (teal) in
35	reference-b.png. There is no other difference.
36	
37	- **reference.png**: a flat 2-logical-pixel navy outline fully enclosing the teal body.
38	  The two top stalks are 4 px wide and therefore rendered entirely in outline colour,
39	  with no teal interior. Two full-width navy bars at y 9..10 and y 26..27 read as a
40	  shoulder line and a base line. Outline is a single flat colour with no ramp.
41	- **reference-b.png**: no outline. Flat teal silhouette, cream eyes only. The shoulder
42	  and base bars and the stalk interiors disappear entirely, because they were drawn in
43	  the outline colour rather than as separate shapes.
44	
45	**Inference, not measurement:** the outline in reference.png is not decorative trim. It
46	carries interior structure (the shoulder bar, the base bar, and the solidity of the
47	stalks). Dropping it, as reference-b.png does, removes readable landmarks, not just the
48	contour. A decision for the unoutlined treatment therefore has to re-author that
49	interior structure in some other way — a second teal value, or a cream accent — rather
50	than simply deleting the outline colour.
51	
52	## Coupling between outline and canvas size, inference
53	
54	A 2 px outline on an 18 x 25 figure spends roughly 46% of the visible pixels (180 of
55	390) on contour and bars. That ratio is a property of the figure's size, so the outline
56	decision and the canvas decision are not independent:
57	
58	- On a canvas materially smaller than 32 x 32, a 2 px outline would leave very little
59	  interior for a scout/medic to differ in, and the two characters would be hard to tell
60	  apart.
61	- On a canvas materially larger than 32 x 32, a 2 px outline thins out visually and
62	  reads closer to a 1 px line at the reference's apparent weight.
63	
64	## What the references do not establish
65	
66	- **Projection.** Both figures are front-facing and symmetric. Neither shows a side
67	  view, which is the stated destination. The references establish colour, edge language,
68	  alpha behaviour and detail density; they do not establish the side-view silhouette,
69	  limb construction, or a facing direction.
70	- **Scout and medic differentiation.** Neither reference carries role-identifying
71	  equipment or a distinguishing accent colour.
72	- **Target display scale, engine, or importer.**
73	- **Animation poses, cycles, directions or timing.**
74

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
26	the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
27	criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
28	**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
29	scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
30	Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
31	A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
32	requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
33	also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
34	explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
35	Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.
36	
37	For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
38	when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
39	uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
40	Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
41	from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
42	assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
43	and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
44	claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.
45	
46	When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
47	critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
48	Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
49	message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
50	Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
51	caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
52	that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
53	child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
54	an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
55	foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
56	depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
57	changing the user's global configuration.
58	
59	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
60	
61	## Specialist → caller while working
62	
63	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
64	
65	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
66	
67	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
68	
69	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.
70	
71	## Caller: review a cold continuation
72	
73	A returned continuation proposes what the caller should consume next, even when
74	it carries forward unchanged state or previously accepted work. Review the
75	current note, proposed next operation and literal request/criteria that will
76	govern that operation. Reading source files and validating the store establish
77	inputs for this comparison; they do not establish that its conclusions follow.
78	
79	1. Recover the original brief, adopted decisions and existing authorization from
80	   their actual sources. Open the returned continuation and the full relevant
81	   saved criteria yourself. Compare inherited clauses as well as new ones. Keep
82	   historical acceptance attached to the candidate and contract it evaluated;
83	   an unchanged hash or earlier passing verdict does not establish a clause's
84	   authority for the next work.
85	
86	2. Save a compact caller comparison covering each consequential claim,
87	   carried-forward restriction and answer effect. For JSON returns, use the
88	   [literal handoff review](handoff-review.md) to inventory the whole question
89	   collection and whole authored next-operation subtree. Review every listed
90	   value; the specialist's worksheet does not choose the coverage. Independently
91	   read the sources and prerequisites. Record **claim or literal criterion;
92	   source and locator; current authority/status; change actually authorized;
93	   actual operation prerequisite; finding and disposition**. Cite the evidence
94	   you interpreted, not the specialist's assurance. Split mixed-authority clauses
95	   and distinguish requirements from permitted defaults or alternatives. If a
96	   rule excludes a plausible alternative, identify whether the source excludes
97	   it or the rule belongs to a narrower expert trial. Preserve required outcomes.
98	
99	3. For each requested answer, independently apply the
100	   [operation-effect check](intake-sample.md#check-what-an-answer-enables): trace
101	   the named task/phase through its outputs, actual or intended contracts and
102	   all linked choices, then its applicable dependency/adoption gates. A missing
103	   contract makes the future choice check conditional; a short current blocker
104	   list does not establish all prerequisites for the proposed operation. Assume
105	   only that answer is supplied. Each other choice keeps its status and scope
106	   unless the answer explicitly adopts it or a cited existing decision already
107	   establishes it. Compare every claimed effect in the question, decision table,
108	   saved note and final response. Matching values or adding an adoption decision
109	   does not confirm other choices. Distinguish a usable contract draft
110	   from task readiness and artwork acceptance. Name the dependencies that remain
111	   without making later production requirements block authorized sample work.
112	
113	4. When this comparison finds a discrepancy, send your own precise finding and
114	   source evidence to the same native specialist. Ask for a corrected current
115	   proposal with an explicit old-to-new explanation, preserving the historical
116	   artifacts and acceptance. Wait for the revision. If the first return is
117	   consistent, record the independent comparison without inventing a correction
118	   round. Do not declare consistency solely because the specialist followed a
119	   checklist, retained earlier bytes or returned a valid state.
120	
121	5. After the last specialist change, reopen the actual final files and current
122	   state, verify their identities and applicable runtime checks, and recheck the
123	   affected claims against the sources. Write your authored result fields from
124	   that review, not a predecessor's values. The new current operation/condition
125	   section must carry all operative instructions; older operational notes remain
126	   history/evidence, not additional instructions adopted by section name. Primary
127	   source criteria and owner requirements still govern.
128	   Run the [literal coverage check](handoff-review.md#check-coverage-then-finish-the-semantic-review)
129	   on your saved result and current instruction excerpts. Independently reopen
130	   the actual fields and text afterward: coverage, matching values and intact
131	   hashes do not establish that their meaning follows from the sources or cover
132	   unlisted prose. Resolve contradictory effects or required/optional conditions
133	   in a new current version and retain prior bytes. Return useful saved progress,
134	   any still necessary direct question and the precise step its answer enables,
135	   with existing authorization and remaining dependencies explicit.
136	
137	## Specialist → caller at completion
138	
139	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
140	PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
141	of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
142	from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below

144	
145	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
146	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
147	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
148	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
149	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
150	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
151	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
152	
153	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
154	
155	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.

# Agent-to-agent asset work

Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.

## Caller → specialist

Supply the smallest complete assignment:

| Context | What the specialist needs |
| --- | --- |
| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |

Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.

For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.

The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.

When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.

For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.

When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
changing the user's global configuration.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Caller: review a cold continuation

A returned continuation proposes what the caller should consume next, even when
it carries forward unchanged state or previously accepted work. Review the
current note, proposed next operation and literal request/criteria that will
govern that operation. Reading source files and validating the store establish
inputs for this comparison; they do not establish that its conclusions follow.

1. Recover the original brief, adopted decisions and existing authorization from
   their actual sources. Open the returned continuation and the full relevant
   saved criteria yourself. Compare inherited clauses as well as new ones. Keep
   historical acceptance attached to the candidate and contract it evaluated;
   an unchanged hash or earlier passing verdict does not establish a clause's
   authority for the next work.

2. Save a compact caller comparison covering each consequential claim,
   carried-forward restriction and answer effect. For JSON returns, use the
   [literal handoff review](handoff-review.md) to inventory the whole question
   collection and whole authored next-operation subtree. Review every listed
   value; the specialist's worksheet does not choose the coverage. Independently
   read the sources and prerequisites. Record **claim or literal criterion;
   source and locator; current authority/status; change actually authorized;
   actual operation prerequisite; finding and disposition**. Cite the evidence
   you interpreted, not the specialist's assurance. Split mixed-authority clauses
   and distinguish requirements from permitted defaults or alternatives. If a
   rule excludes a plausible alternative, identify whether the source excludes
   it or the rule belongs to a narrower expert trial. Preserve required outcomes.

3. For each requested answer, independently apply the
   [operation-effect check](intake-sample.md#check-what-an-answer-enables): trace
   the named task/phase through its outputs, actual or intended contracts and
   all linked choices, then its applicable dependency/adoption gates. A missing
   contract makes the future choice check conditional; a short current blocker
   list does not establish all prerequisites for the proposed operation. Assume
   only that answer is supplied. Each other choice keeps its status and scope
   unless the answer explicitly adopts it or a cited existing decision already
   establishes it. Compare every claimed effect in the question, decision table,
   saved note and final response. Matching values or adding an adoption decision
   does not confirm other choices. Distinguish a usable contract draft
   from task readiness and artwork acceptance. Name the dependencies that remain
   without making later production requirements block authorized sample work.

4. When this comparison finds a discrepancy, send your own precise finding and
   source evidence to the same native specialist. Ask for a corrected current
   proposal with an explicit old-to-new explanation, preserving the historical
   artifacts and acceptance. Wait for the revision. If the first return is
   consistent, record the independent comparison without inventing a correction
   round. Do not declare consistency solely because the specialist followed a
   checklist, retained earlier bytes or returned a valid state.

5. After the last specialist change, reopen the actual final files and current
   state, verify their identities and applicable runtime checks, and recheck the
   affected claims against the sources. Write your authored result fields from
   that review, not a predecessor's values. The new current operation/condition
   section must carry all operative instructions; older operational notes remain
   history/evidence, not additional instructions adopted by section name. Primary
   source criteria and owner requirements still govern.
   Run the [literal coverage check](handoff-review.md#check-coverage-then-finish-the-semantic-review)
   on your saved result and current instruction excerpts. Independently reopen
   the actual fields and text afterward: coverage, matching values and intact
   hashes do not establish that their meaning follows from the sources or cover
   unlisted prose. Resolve contradictory effects or required/optional conditions
   in a new current version and retain prior bytes. Return useful saved progress,
   any still necessary direct question and the precise step its answer enables,
   with existing authorization and remaining dependencies explicit.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
without manufacturing PLAR or production records:

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.

Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.

The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.

For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --path QUEUE --asset ID
--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --view caller --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
Return the caller view and its exact handoff locator; the caller opens the retained
file and compares its state identity with fresh focused PLAR. Omitting `--view caller`
keeps the existing receipt response. The view does not add acceptance or alter the
saved handoff. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.

`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.

Use optional `details.caller` for the bounded ordinary return: summary, artifact
and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
not automatically summarized.

For example, only when the assigned destination inspection remains unperformed:

```json
{
  "status": "partial",
  "caller": {
    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
    "integration": {
      "status": "not_performed",
      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
    },
    "issues": [
      {
        "category": "unfinished_work",
        "summary": "The assigned destination check has not run.",
        "recovery": "Run the assigned destination check, retain its actual evidence and refresh the handoff."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Use actual findings and omit inapplicable fields. Summary/recovery text is bounded
to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each
hold at most 12 entries, and the complete caller block at most 8192 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes. Move detail to linked files instead of truncating obligations.
Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
`not_in_scope`; omission is not one of those observations.

Follow the returned full-handoff, details and resume locators for exact retrieval.
Read `resume_inline`: the unchanged `resume` is present up to 4096 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes; otherwise `resume_ref` retrieves it in full. It is never rewritten or
truncated. `details_ref` and `resume_ref` identify physical source ranges and JSON
pointers in the same immutable handoff. Use its `path`/`sha256` for the full file.
These facts describe the captured selection; use the returned `refresh` read
after source or state changes, and reconcile the current identities. Read that full resume before acting on its jobs or
recovery instructions. Keep routine responses useful without pasting the complete
criteria audit, request report or tool transcript into the return.

On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.

Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.

1	# Intake through a reviewed representative sample
2	
3	Use this operation for an incomplete brief, a consequential artistic uncertainty, or the first representative item/pose/cycle/neighborhood before producing a family. Follow the [production profile](../../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). This reference governs PIXL operation; maintaining this repository remains a development task.
4	
5	## Required context and entry
6	
7	Read the actual [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) and [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). New lifecycle projects use `intake STORE --name NAME --brief TEXT --root PROJECT_ROOT`, or `pixl_intake`. It creates a project and actors without a style contract. Existing PX1 state keeps its version; `workflow` deliberately rejects it. Do not relabel an old header, invent past confirmation, or discard old evidence to migrate it.
8	
9	Inspect available references and artifacts at native scale and enlarged scale. Identify which choices affect this operation and which can remain unresolved. Preserve the user's actual instruction or relevant observation in project-owned source files, then record S identities/ranges. The profile supplies the judgment; dimensions, binary alpha and fixed palettes are not universal requirements.
10	
11	## Keep authority through derived rules
12	
13	Before deriving a style contract, acceptance criterion, checker rule or provider instruction, retain a compact account of each consequential restriction: property/value, authority and status, exact supporting instruction or adopted project choice, and where the restriction applies. Use the existing choice/source fields in PIXL state; this account adds no UDL fields. Carry its status through the entire approach, including prompts, checks and handoff.
14	
15	The user's instruction and adopted project choices establish requirements. Reference pixels establish observations; matching a reference does not adopt every measured dimension, color, gap, alpha level or component count as a mandatory rule. For an unspecified property, explain a project-specific proposal and the trial it would test. A proposed trial can proceed within existing authorization while the final production choice remains open.
16	
17	A supplied palette expressed as color roles or families preserves those choices without automatically making sampled reference hex values an exclusive allowed-color list. Use exact working colors as a scoped proposal when useful; attribute exact restrictions to the owner only when their instruction or adoption establishes them. Binary transparency constrains alpha, while opaque edge colors and anti-aliasing require their own authority. Keep these distinctions in the saved contract and criteria, and continue the authorized sample work without asking the caller to repeat settled choices.
18	
19	If your interpretation of an image differs from the brief's terminology, describe the observed pixels and the uncertainty while preserving the requested treatment. An alternative that contradicts that treatment is a change for the user to adopt, not a correction you can silently install in the contract. Neither a tool default nor a passing checker supplies that adoption.
20	
21	Keep diagnostic conclusions attached to their tested artifact, method, scale and background. Failure of one resized fixture does not establish a minimum canvas for other designs; a measured component count or contrast ratio does not establish a universal rejection threshold. Label verified tool limitations separately from artistic choices.
22	
23	Before saving the approach or a verdict, trace every enforced artistic restriction back to that account. Correct downstream claims such as “approved,” “binding,” or “must” when their source is still observed, proposed or unresolved. Preserve the earlier draft and its evidence when correcting it.
24	
25	For a selected PLAR asset's first concrete candidate, use [PLAR preparation](../../plar/references/prepare.md) to save the reviewed output/criteria plan and first durable request in one operation. The record-level sequence below remains available for advanced plans and explicit amendments.
26	
27	## Preserve intake and plan before execution
28	
29	1. Load the current state and canonical hash. Decode it through the runner, keeping `format: 2` in the host adapter. Amend the relevant fields, increase the revision by one, encode a candidate, validate against the project root, and commit with the previously observed hash. A stale-write error means reload and reconcile.
30	2. Add each consequential choice as I with project, actor, key, status, value, sources and rationale; add it to P.in. Unknown values are null. Observations, proposals and confirmations remain different statuses. Preserve conflicting alternatives instead of selecting a scaffold default.
31	3. Research the uncertain technique through the [knowledge operation](knowledge.md). A K recipe or reference POC is useful context, not a proof for this asset. A research/sample T can use unproven K and have `dc=[]`; it does not need a fabricated D. Adoption into production/delivery needs the specified decision and applicable proofs.
32	4. Name the smallest useful sample as F, owned by its T. Separate T.ip inputs, T.op planned outputs and T.ca actual nominated candidates. Before a file exists, F is the output plan; do not create a false X path/hash. Instantiate a concrete C only from usable observed/proposed/confirmed choices. Link those choices through C.ch. An unresolved canvas can remain I while a raster F has no C and its sample task is blocked.
33	5. Declare Q criteria appropriate to the question and destination. Include explicit observable conditions, domain and required evidence mode. Mechanical properties, visual readability, temporal/neighbor continuity and engine behavior are separate where applicable. Do not add irrelevant gates to a report or impose a universal art style. Save this plan before interpreting candidate results: new pass/fail verdicts require the same plan and semantic scope in the prior saved revision.
34	
35	The bundled [incomplete intake example](../../../resources/examples/intake/project.px) shows declared choices, a planned output and requirements without a fabricated artifact. It is a syntax example, not a project-approved style or a finished sample.
36	
37	Host adapter example for one unresolved choice (add a real P reference and actor; this is one record, not a complete document):
38	
39	```json
40	{"id":"canvas","kind":"I","fields":{"pr":{"$ref":"project"},"wh":{"$ref":"user"},"ky":"px","st":{"$symbol":"unresolved"},"vl":null,"so":[],"wy":"The final canvas size has not been chosen."}}
41	```
42	
43	Use symbols and references as tagged values. Wire literal byte counts come from `encode`, not hand counting. A confirmed choice needs supporting S; a proposal can retain a rationale before evidence exists. Available record hashes come from `validate`, so E bindings use actual canonical identities rather than guessed digests.
44	
45	## Produce, inspect and retain the candidate
46	
47	Run `workflow STATE --root PROJECT_ROOT` or `pixl_workflow`. Resolve only the task's actual blockers. Sample work can investigate a proposed contract; production/delivery cannot treat that proposal as confirmed. Use the [production procedure](production.md) for authorized real tool execution. Missing tools leave the plan and local work useful; they do not supply a generated asset.
48	
49	Retrieve the actual candidate and store it under a new project-owned path. Record X with its byte hash, matching contract/kind, and `of` pointing to F. Nominate it through T.ca. Preserve older candidates when revising. Run applicable measurements, visually inspect the actual file/reference comparison, and execute required engine checks when available. Record an unavailable engine check as unavailable, not a pass or an artistic failure.
50	
51	For a saved raster candidate, use the [candidate inspection operation](inspection.md) to prepare exact native/enlarged views and retain an explicitly supplied review. It resolves the current plan and publishes the observation report with the required E/V bindings. The host still needs to view the actual images; preparation alone is unperformed review.
52	
53	For evidence outside that operation, retain the actual observation file and create E with its hash, timestamp, outcome, mode and full semantic bindings for both X and Q. Those bindings include the plan, contract, linked choices and sources. Then add V naming the task/candidate/criterion, reviewer, status, reason and E references; retain it in T.vr. `workflow` shows any absent verdict as unperformed. A local size/palette measurement cannot satisfy a Q requiring visual or live evidence.
54	
55	An unavailable V has `ev=[]` and a concrete reason. For example, a target project is absent, so its import behavior remains unknown. A failed V retains what was actually wrong. A current passing V is only the result for its exact candidate and criterion. Generic encoding cannot determine whether a claimed visual review truly occurred; the acting agent must inspect before making that claim.
56	
57	## Revise, finish or leave a resumable boundary
58	
59	- If a candidate fails, keep X/E/V, create the revised X and nominate it. Evaluate the new candidate against the saved criteria; it cannot borrow old bindings.
60	- If correcting a verdict, supersede the old V with `ob=true` and add a new V. Do not rewrite its previous outcome or reviewer. Supersede E only when its own observation is invalidated or replaced.
61	- If the plan, relevant choice or contract changes, preserve the change rationale/sources, reopen affected completed work, and supersede stale E/V. Commit the changed plan before publishing new evaluation. Do not merely recompute old receipt hashes.
62	- After all saved criteria pass, use `task-complete STORE TASK CANDIDATE... --expect HASH --root ROOT` or `pixl_task_complete` to nominate the explicit accepted candidates and finish the task. It validates existing acceptance, preserves every failed candidate/verdict, and publishes the legal state transitions; it does not supply a missing review. Read `workflow` afterward to confirm the durable result. [Operation contract](../../../resources/spec/task-completion.md).
63	- Mark T done only when all its nominated outputs satisfy every declared criterion and all prerequisite tasks are done. A mechanically valid but visually rejected sample stays unfinished. Deliver useful files while keeping an unavailable engine requirement explicit; do not label them fully accepted for that destination.
64	- Commit state and leave a handoff with the next task or unresolved requirement. A cold session starts with `workflow` and the focused `context`, inspecting retained observations before repeating work.
65	
66	This operation ends with either a representative sample accepted against its actual requirements, or a concrete retained boundary: missing choice, failed candidate, unavailable inspection, or next proof. Explain that useful outcome plainly; keep hashes, record IDs and mechanical details in evidence unless they clarify a conflict.
67	
68	If the next dependent step needs a consequential user choice, the final response must contain the useful progress saved, a direct concise question for the smallest set of necessary answers, and what those answers unlock. Address that question to the caller: a list of decisions needed or next steps once answered does not itself ask for the choice. Carry a still-unanswered question into that final response even when it was asked earlier or saved in the handoff. Present genuine alternatives when helpful and keep suggested trials labeled as proposals. Reference dimensions remain observations until adopted for this project. Continue authorized work that is independent of the answer. When the necessary choices are already supplied, use them and report the next operation under the existing authorization.
69	
70	## Check what an answer enables
71	
72	Name the next operation, its task and phase before claiming what an answer
73	unlocks. Read `workflow STATE --root ROOT` and
74	`context STATE TASK --view authoring --root ROOT` (or `pixl_workflow` and
75	`pixl_context` with that task as `focus` and `view="authoring"`). Keep the state
76	identity with this check. The workflow describes the saved plan, not every
77	possible future contract.
78	
79	Trace each planned output through **T.op → F.ct → C.ch → I**, reading the linked
80	choices' actual status, value, source and scope. When an output has no contract,
81	its current blockers cannot enumerate the choices a future contract would link.
82	Identify the intended contract and its links, or mark that future operation
83	conditional until they are selected. Inspect relevant `other_intake` entries;
84	unlinked choices are not automatically irrelevant. Do not drop applicable choice
85	links to make a readiness check pass.
86	
87	For production/delivery activation, account for completed task prerequisites,
88	concrete raster contracts, confirmation of every choice in those output

# Intake through a reviewed representative sample

Use this operation for an incomplete brief, a consequential artistic uncertainty, or the first representative item/pose/cycle/neighborhood before producing a family. Follow the [production profile](../../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). This reference governs PIXL operation; maintaining this repository remains a development task.

## Required context and entry

Read the actual [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) and [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). New lifecycle projects use `intake STORE --name NAME --brief TEXT --root PROJECT_ROOT`, or `pixl_intake`. It creates a project and actors without a style contract. Existing PX1 state keeps its version; `workflow` deliberately rejects it. Do not relabel an old header, invent past confirmation, or discard old evidence to migrate it.

Inspect available references and artifacts at native scale and enlarged scale. Identify which choices affect this operation and which can remain unresolved. Preserve the user's actual instruction or relevant observation in project-owned source files, then record S identities/ranges. The profile supplies the judgment; dimensions, binary alpha and fixed palettes are not universal requirements.

## Keep authority through derived rules

Before deriving a style contract, acceptance criterion, checker rule or provider instruction, retain a compact account of each consequential restriction: property/value, authority and status, exact supporting instruction or adopted project choice, and where the restriction applies. Use the existing choice/source fields in PIXL state; this account adds no UDL fields. Carry its status through the entire approach, including prompts, checks and handoff.

The user's instruction and adopted project choices establish requirements. Reference pixels establish observations; matching a reference does not adopt every measured dimension, color, gap, alpha level or component count as a mandatory rule. For an unspecified property, explain a project-specific proposal and the trial it would test. A proposed trial can proceed within existing authorization while the final production choice remains open.

A supplied palette expressed as color roles or families preserves those choices without automatically making sampled reference hex values an exclusive allowed-color list. Use exact working colors as a scoped proposal when useful; attribute exact restrictions to the owner only when their instruction or adoption establishes them. Binary transparency constrains alpha, while opaque edge colors and anti-aliasing require their own authority. Keep these distinctions in the saved contract and criteria, and continue the authorized sample work without asking the caller to repeat settled choices.

If your interpretation of an image differs from the brief's terminology, describe the observed pixels and the uncertainty while preserving the requested treatment. An alternative that contradicts that treatment is a change for the user to adopt, not a correction you can silently install in the contract. Neither a tool default nor a passing checker supplies that adoption.

Keep diagnostic conclusions attached to their tested artifact, method, scale and background. Failure of one resized fixture does not establish a minimum canvas for other designs; a measured component count or contrast ratio does not establish a universal rejection threshold. Label verified tool limitations separately from artistic choices.

Before saving the approach or a verdict, trace every enforced artistic restriction back to that account. Correct downstream claims such as “approved,” “binding,” or “must” when their source is still observed, proposed or unresolved. Preserve the earlier draft and its evidence when correcting it.

For a selected PLAR asset's first concrete candidate, use [PLAR preparation](../../plar/references/prepare.md) to save the reviewed output/criteria plan and first durable request in one operation. The record-level sequence below remains available for advanced plans and explicit amendments.

## Preserve intake and plan before execution

1. Load the current state and canonical hash. Decode it through the runner, keeping `format: 2` in the host adapter. Amend the relevant fields, increase the revision by one, encode a candidate, validate against the project root, and commit with the previously observed hash. A stale-write error means reload and reconcile.
2. Add each consequential choice as I with project, actor, key, status, value, sources and rationale; add it to P.in. Unknown values are null. Observations, proposals and confirmations remain different statuses. Preserve conflicting alternatives instead of selecting a scaffold default.
3. Research the uncertain technique through the [knowledge operation](knowledge.md). A K recipe or reference POC is useful context, not a proof for this asset. A research/sample T can use unproven K and have `dc=[]`; it does not need a fabricated D. Adoption into production/delivery needs the specified decision and applicable proofs.
4. Name the smallest useful sample as F, owned by its T. Separate T.ip inputs, T.op planned outputs and T.ca actual nominated candidates. Before a file exists, F is the output plan; do not create a false X path/hash. Instantiate a concrete C only from usable observed/proposed/confirmed choices. Link those choices through C.ch. An unresolved canvas can remain I while a raster F has no C and its sample task is blocked.
5. Declare Q criteria appropriate to the question and destination. Include explicit observable conditions, domain and required evidence mode. Mechanical properties, visual readability, temporal/neighbor continuity and engine behavior are separate where applicable. Do not add irrelevant gates to a report or impose a universal art style. Save this plan before interpreting candidate results: new pass/fail verdicts require the same plan and semantic scope in the prior saved revision.

The bundled [incomplete intake example](../../../resources/examples/intake/project.px) shows declared choices, a planned output and requirements without a fabricated artifact. It is a syntax example, not a project-approved style or a finished sample.

Host adapter example for one unresolved choice (add a real P reference and actor; this is one record, not a complete document):

```json
{"id":"canvas","kind":"I","fields":{"pr":{"$ref":"project"},"wh":{"$ref":"user"},"ky":"px","st":{"$symbol":"unresolved"},"vl":null,"so":[],"wy":"The final canvas size has not been chosen."}}
```

Use symbols and references as tagged values. Wire literal byte counts come from `encode`, not hand counting. A confirmed choice needs supporting S; a proposal can retain a rationale before evidence exists. Available record hashes come from `validate`, so E bindings use actual canonical identities rather than guessed digests.

## Produce, inspect and retain the candidate

Run `workflow STATE --root PROJECT_ROOT` or `pixl_workflow`. Resolve only the task's actual blockers. Sample work can investigate a proposed contract; production/delivery cannot treat that proposal as confirmed. Use the [production procedure](production.md) for authorized real tool execution. Missing tools leave the plan and local work useful; they do not supply a generated asset.

Retrieve the actual candidate and store it under a new project-owned path. Record X with its byte hash, matching contract/kind, and `of` pointing to F. Nominate it through T.ca. Preserve older candidates when revising. Run applicable measurements, visually inspect the actual file/reference comparison, and execute required engine checks when available. Record an unavailable engine check as unavailable, not a pass or an artistic failure.

For a saved raster candidate, use the [candidate inspection operation](inspection.md) to prepare exact native/enlarged views and retain an explicitly supplied review. It resolves the current plan and publishes the observation report with the required E/V bindings. The host still needs to view the actual images; preparation alone is unperformed review.

For evidence outside that operation, retain the actual observation file and create E with its hash, timestamp, outcome, mode and full semantic bindings for both X and Q. Those bindings include the plan, contract, linked choices and sources. Then add V naming the task/candidate/criterion, reviewer, status, reason and E references; retain it in T.vr. `workflow` shows any absent verdict as unperformed. A local size/palette measurement cannot satisfy a Q requiring visual or live evidence.

An unavailable V has `ev=[]` and a concrete reason. For example, a target project is absent, so its import behavior remains unknown. A failed V retains what was actually wrong. A current passing V is only the result for its exact candidate and criterion. Generic encoding cannot determine whether a claimed visual review truly occurred; the acting agent must inspect before making that claim.

## Revise, finish or leave a resumable boundary

- If a candidate fails, keep X/E/V, create the revised X and nominate it. Evaluate the new candidate against the saved criteria; it cannot borrow old bindings.
- If correcting a verdict, supersede the old V with `ob=true` and add a new V. Do not rewrite its previous outcome or reviewer. Supersede E only when its own observation is invalidated or replaced.
- If the plan, relevant choice or contract changes, preserve the change rationale/sources, reopen affected completed work, and supersede stale E/V. Commit the changed plan before publishing new evaluation. Do not merely recompute old receipt hashes.
- After all saved criteria pass, use `task-complete STORE TASK CANDIDATE... --expect HASH --root ROOT` or `pixl_task_complete` to nominate the explicit accepted candidates and finish the task. It validates existing acceptance, preserves every failed candidate/verdict, and publishes the legal state transitions; it does not supply a missing review. Read `workflow` afterward to confirm the durable result. [Operation contract](../../../resources/spec/task-completion.md).
- Mark T done only when all its nominated outputs satisfy every declared criterion and all prerequisite tasks are done. A mechanically valid but visually rejected sample stays unfinished. Deliver useful files while keeping an unavailable engine requirement explicit; do not label them fully accepted for that destination.
- Commit state and leave a handoff with the next task or unresolved requirement. A cold session starts with `workflow` and the focused `context`, inspecting retained observations before repeating work.

This operation ends with either a representative sample accepted against its actual requirements, or a concrete retained boundary: missing choice, failed candidate, unavailable inspection, or next proof. Explain that useful outcome plainly; keep hashes, record IDs and mechanical details in evidence unless they clarify a conflict.

If the next dependent step needs a consequential user choice, the final response must contain the useful progress saved, a direct concise question for the smallest set of necessary answers, and what those answers unlock. Address that question to the caller: a list of decisions needed or next steps once answered does not itself ask for the choice. Carry a still-unanswered question into that final response even when it was asked earlier or saved in the handoff. Present genuine alternatives when helpful and keep suggested trials labeled as proposals. Reference dimensions remain observations until adopted for this project. Continue authorized work that is independent of the answer. When the necessary choices are already supplied, use them and report the next operation under the existing authorization.

## Check what an answer enables

Name the next operation, its task and phase before claiming what an answer
unlocks. Read `workflow STATE --root ROOT` and
`context STATE TASK --view authoring --root ROOT` (or `pixl_workflow` and
`pixl_context` with that task as `focus` and `view="authoring"`). Keep the state
identity with this check. The workflow describes the saved plan, not every
possible future contract.

Trace each planned output through **T.op → F.ct → C.ch → I**, reading the linked
choices' actual status, value, source and scope. When an output has no contract,
its current blockers cannot enumerate the choices a future contract would link.
Identify the intended contract and its links, or mark that future operation
conditional until they are selected. Inspect relevant `other_intake` entries;
unlinked choices are not automatically irrelevant. Do not drop applicable choice
links to make a readiness check pass.

For production/delivery activation, account for completed task prerequisites,
concrete raster contracts, confirmation of every choice in those output
contracts, and the task's evidence-backed adoption decision. Check passing method
proofs when the task links knowledge, and baseline/destination gates when its
family plan declares them. Retrieve complete context when the authoring view
omits proof receipts. Read the source and proof scope of an adoption decision;
its existence does not confirm linked choices or establish its relevance to the
proposed work. Report only applicable missing prerequisites, not every possible
future gate or every intake choice in the project.

In the saved decision table, project **only the supplied answer**: the exact
choice/contract change it supports, its authority and scope, the operation that
becomes available, and the prerequisites that remain. Keep other statuses and
scope unchanged. Drafting a contract, activating a production task and accepting
its artwork are different outcomes. A future projection is conditional reasoning,
not a fresh readiness result; after authorized changes are actually saved, rerun
workflow before claiming current readiness. Provider availability and required
visual/engine acceptance remain separate.

### Write the current effect before the return

Use this worksheet inside the new continuation note for each consequential answer
effect or claimed blocker. Shared prerequisite rows may be referenced rather than
repeated. It is a reasoning aid, not new PIXL syntax or proof of a correct review.

```text
Current operation and answer effects
State/plan identity:
Operation and phase:
Question (or "no owner answer needed for this operation"):
Assume only this answer:

Prerequisite or permitted alternative | Source + locator | Current status | After only this answer | Still required

Current effect sentence:
Remaining prerequisites:
Authorized default/alternative (or none established):
Current carriers: note section; authored result field/JSON pointer; final wording
Prior instruction superseded: note/section + reason (when applicable)
```

1. Fill the rows from the actual source and prerequisite trace above. Keep every
   unasked choice unchanged. Preserve source-defined alternatives: an allowed
   default and an owner-supplied value are alternative routes, not two mandatory
   inputs. An unknown future contract remains conditional.
2. Write the effect sentence from the completed rows. If anything needed for the
   claimed operation remains, name the narrower step available and the remaining
   requirements; do not say the answer clears the operation's gates. Do not treat
   an answer as completion of a prerequisite whose required work or evidence
   remains missing, or as confirmation of an unasked choice.
3. Make the current operation/condition section self-contained: carry every
   instruction governing that operation, including permitted alternatives.
   Old operational notes remain history/evidence, not parallel current
   instructions, even when linked by section. Cite unchanged sources and facts
   without duplicating history. Correct prior agent interpretations explicitly;
   the new note cannot supersede owner requirements or source criteria.
4. Build authored `question`, `necessary_for`, `unlocks`, `next` and `blocked_on`
   fields from these fresh checked statements, preserving their conditions and
   alternatives. Do not initialize their meaning from an old result's fields.
   Keep runtime-derived continuation unchanged; put authored explanation beside it.
5. For a saved JSON result, perform the [literal handoff review](handoff-review.md):
   inventory the whole question collection and whole authored next-operation
   subtree, review every listed value and bind the complete current instruction
   excerpts. Start with `python -B -I KIT/scripts/check_handoff.py RESULT --root ROOT --scope /remaining_questions --scope /next_action`, using the actual field names.
   Reopen the saved fields and current text after the coverage check and compare
   their meaning with the sources. Coverage is not semantic acceptance. Use the
   source-checked effect, with remaining requirements, in the final response.

Use this check to ask only for information needed by the immediate dependent
operation. Existing source-backed decisions and authorization still apply; later
production requirements do not block an independently useful sample or local
plan. Keep the detailed trace in the note and return the useful next action and
its material remaining dependencies plainly.

## Cold intake handoff

1. Read the complete production profile and this procedure. Start with the saved
   workflow and focused context, then inspect the sources behind claimed blockers.
   Recover owner decisions and authorization separately from the predecessor's
   proposals, visual judgments and measurements. A diagnostic finding remains
   scoped to its tested artifact; it does not decide the owner's aesthetic or
   establish a requirement for a newly authored asset. Preserve earlier reports
   and identify overbroad inferences in the continuation.

2. Save the [current-effect worksheet](#write-the-current-effect-before-the-return)
   in a new continuation note. Include observed/proposed choices with their real
   authority, source and scope; unasked rows keep their status. A diagnostic can
   support a recommendation without deciding for the owner. Keep the current
   operation section self-contained and continue independent useful work.

3. Apply [the operation-effect check](#check-what-an-answer-enables) to the
   next local operation and any later operation the handoff claims to unlock.
   Trace the proposed contract's linked choices even when that contract is not
   yet saved. Keep its remaining phase/adoption dependencies explicit; preserve
   existing authorization and continue independent sample or planning work.

4. Use the checked note to finish with saved progress, a direct concise question
   addressed to the caller, and the exact local operation its answer unlocks.
   A decision list or a statement that the owner should choose does not ask the
   question. If the necessary choices are already supplied, use them and state
   the next operation without asking again. Keep supporting diagnostics in the
   note; carry their scope and authority into any claim repeated in the response.

When the representative sample is accepted and the assignment continues across a family, enter the [family and delivery operation](family-delivery.md). It records the exact nominated sample as the baseline, saves member and destination plans, and declares collective continuity before batch results. Replaced/rejected samples and unknown provider attempts must be reconciled before dependent production; an old artifact's existence is not baseline eligibility.

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
26	the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
27	criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
28	**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
29	scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
30	Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
31	A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
32	requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
33	also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
34	explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
35	Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.
36	
37	For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
38	when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
39	uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
40	Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
41	from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
42	assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
43	and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
44	claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.
45	
46	When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
47	critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
48	Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
49	message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
50	Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
51	caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
52	that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
53	child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
54	an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
55	foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
56	depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
57	changing the user's global configuration.
58	
59	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
60

62	
63	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

67	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
68	
69	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison.
