123	   affected claims against the sources. Write your authored result fields from
124	   that review, not a predecessor's values. The new current operation/condition
125	   section must carry all operative instructions; older operational notes remain
126	   history/evidence, not additional instructions adopted by section name. Primary
127	   source criteria and owner requirements still govern.
128	   Run the [literal coverage check](handoff-review.md#check-coverage-then-finish-the-semantic-review)
129	   on your saved result and current instruction excerpts. Independently reopen
130	   the actual fields and text afterward: coverage, matching values and intact
131	   hashes do not establish that their meaning follows from the sources or cover
132	   unlisted prose. Resolve contradictory effects or required/optional conditions
133	   in a new current version and retain prior bytes. Return useful saved progress,
134	   any still necessary direct question and the precise step its answer enables,
135	   with existing authorization and remaining dependencies explicit.
136	
137	## Specialist → caller at completion
138	
139	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
140	PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
141	of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
142	from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
143	without manufacturing PLAR or production records:
144	
145	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
146	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
147	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
148	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
149	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
150	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
151	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
152	
153	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
154	
155	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.
156	
157	Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.
158	
159	The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.
160	
161	For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
162	use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
163	`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
164	selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
165	CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --path QUEUE --asset ID
166	--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --view caller --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
167	complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
168	Return the caller view and its exact handoff locator; the caller opens the retained
169	file and compares its state identity with fresh focused PLAR. Omitting `--view caller`
170	keeps the existing receipt response. The view does not add acceptance or alter the
171	saved handoff. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
172	Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
173	Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
174	requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
175	active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
176	when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.
177	
178	`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
179	expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
180	caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
181	`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
182	runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
183	The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
184	does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.
185	
186	Use optional `details.caller` for the bounded ordinary return: summary, artifact
187	and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
188	[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
189	in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
190	contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
191	confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
192	judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
193	these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
194	A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
195	not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
196	`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
197	not automatically summarized.
198	
199	For example, only when the assigned destination inspection remains unperformed:
200	
201	```json
202	{
203	  "status": "partial",
204	  "caller": {
205	    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
206	    "integration": {
207	      "status": "not_performed",
208	      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
209	    },
210	    "issues": [
211	      {
212	        "category": "unfinished_work",
213	        "summary": "The assigned destination check has not run.",
214	        "recovery": "Run the assigned destination check, retain its actual evidence and refresh the handoff."
215	      }
216	    ]
217	  }
218	}
219	```
220	
221	Use actual findings and omit inapplicable fields. Summary/recovery text is bounded
222	to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each
223	hold at most 12 entries, and the complete caller block at most 8192 compact UTF-8
224	JSON bytes. Move detail to linked files instead of truncating obligations.
225	Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
226	`not_in_scope`; omission is not one of those observations.
227	
228	Follow the returned full-handoff, details and resume locators for exact retrieval.
229	Read `resume_inline`: the unchanged `resume` is present up to 4096 compact UTF-8
230	JSON bytes; otherwise `resume_ref` retrieves it in full. It is never rewritten or
231	truncated. `details_ref` and `resume_ref` identify physical source ranges and JSON
232	pointers in the same immutable handoff. Use its `path`/`sha256` for the full file.
233	These facts describe the captured selection; use the returned `refresh` read
234	after source or state changes, and reconcile the current identities. Read that full resume before acting on its jobs or
235	recovery instructions. Keep routine responses useful without pasting the complete
236	criteria audit, request report or tool transcript into the return.
237	
238	On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
239	requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
240	its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
241	actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
242	explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.
243	
244	Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.
245

1	# Intake through a reviewed representative sample
2	
3	Use this operation for an incomplete brief, a consequential artistic uncertainty, or the first representative item/pose/cycle/neighborhood before producing a family. Follow the [production profile](../../../resources/agent/PROFILE.md). This reference governs PIXL operation; maintaining this repository remains a development task.
4	
5	## Required context and entry
6	
7	Read the actual [PX2 specification](../../../resources/spec/PIXL-2.md) and [registry](../../../runtime/pixl/registry-v2.json). New lifecycle projects use `intake STORE --name NAME --brief TEXT --root PROJECT_ROOT`, or `pixl_intake`. It creates a project and actors without a style contract. Existing PX1 state keeps its version; `workflow` deliberately rejects it. Do not relabel an old header, invent past confirmation, or discard old evidence to migrate it.
8	
9	Inspect available references and artifacts at native scale and enlarged scale. Identify which choices affect this operation and which can remain unresolved. Preserve the user's actual instruction or relevant observation in project-owned source files, then record S identities/ranges. The profile supplies the judgment; dimensions, binary alpha and fixed palettes are not universal requirements.
10	
11	## Keep authority through derived rules
12	
13	Before deriving a style contract, acceptance criterion, checker rule or provider instruction, retain a compact account of each consequential restriction: property/value, authority and status, exact supporting instruction or adopted project choice, and where the restriction applies. Use the existing choice/source fields in PIXL state; this account adds no UDL fields. Carry its status through the entire approach, including prompts, checks and handoff.
14	
15	The user's instruction and adopted project choices establish requirements. Reference pixels establish observations; matching a reference does not adopt every measured dimension, color, gap, alpha level or component count as a mandatory rule. For an unspecified property, explain a project-specific proposal and the trial it would test. A proposed trial can proceed within existing authorization while the final production choice remains open.
16	
17	A supplied palette expressed as color roles or families preserves those choices without automatically making sampled reference hex values an exclusive allowed-color list. Use exact working colors as a scoped proposal when useful; attribute exact restrictions to the owner only when their instruction or adoption establishes them. Binary transparency constrains alpha, while opaque edge colors and anti-aliasing require their own authority. Keep these distinctions in the saved contract and criteria, and continue the authorized sample work without asking the caller to repeat settled choices.
18	
19	If your interpretation of an image differs from the brief's terminology, describe the observed pixels and the uncertainty while preserving the requested treatment. An alternative that contradicts that treatment is a change for the user to adopt, not a correction you can silently install in the contract. Neither a tool default nor a passing checker supplies that adoption.
20	
21	Keep diagnostic conclusions attached to their tested artifact, method, scale and background. Failure of one resized fixture does not establish a minimum canvas for other designs; a measured component count or contrast ratio does not establish a universal rejection threshold. Label verified tool limitations separately from artistic choices.
22	
23	Before saving the approach or a verdict, trace every enforced artistic restriction back to that account. Correct downstream claims such as “approved,” “binding,” or “must” when their source is still observed, proposed or unresolved. Preserve the earlier draft and its evidence when correcting it.
24	
25	For a selected PLAR asset's first concrete candidate, use [PLAR preparation](../../plar/references/prepare.md) to save the reviewed output/criteria plan and first durable request in one operation. The record-level sequence below remains available for advanced plans and explicit amendments.
26	
27	## Preserve intake and plan before execution
28	
29	1. Load the current state and canonical hash. Decode it through the runner, keeping `format: 2` in the host adapter. Amend the relevant fields, increase the revision by one, encode a candidate, validate against the project root, and commit with the previously observed hash. A stale-write error means reload and reconcile.
30	2. Add each consequential choice as I with project, actor, key, status, value, sources and rationale; add it to P.in. Unknown values are null. Observations, proposals and confirmations remain different statuses. Preserve conflicting alternatives instead of selecting a scaffold default.
31	3. Research the uncertain technique through the [knowledge operation](knowledge.md). A K recipe or reference POC is useful context, not a proof for this asset. A research/sample T can use unproven K and have `dc=[]`; it does not need a fabricated D. Adoption into production/delivery needs the specified decision and applicable proofs.
32	4. Name the smallest useful sample as F, owned by its T. Separate T.ip inputs, T.op planned outputs and T.ca actual nominated candidates. Before a file exists, F is the output plan; do not create a false X path/hash. Instantiate a concrete C only from usable observed/proposed/confirmed choices. Link those choices through C.ch. An unresolved canvas can remain I while a raster F has no C and its sample task is blocked.
33	5. Declare Q criteria appropriate to the question and destination. Include explicit observable conditions, domain and required evidence mode. Mechanical properties, visual readability, temporal/neighbor continuity and engine behavior are separate where applicable. Do not add irrelevant gates to a report or impose a universal art style. Save this plan before interpreting candidate results: new pass/fail verdicts require the same plan and semantic scope in the prior saved revision.
34	
35	The bundled [incomplete intake example](../../../resources/examples/intake/project.px) shows declared choices, a planned output and requirements without a fabricated artifact. It is a syntax example, not a project-approved style or a finished sample.
36	
37	Host adapter example for one unresolved choice (add a real P reference and actor; this is one record, not a complete document):
38	
39	```json
40	{"id":"canvas","kind":"I","fields":{"pr":{"$ref":"project"},"wh":{"$ref":"user"},"ky":"px","st":{"$symbol":"unresolved"},"vl":null,"so":[],"wy":"The final canvas size has not been chosen."}}
41	```
42	
43	Use symbols and references as tagged values. Wire literal byte counts come from `encode`, not hand counting. A confirmed choice needs supporting S; a proposal can retain a rationale before evidence exists. Available record hashes come from `validate`, so E bindings use actual canonical identities rather than guessed digests.
44	
45	## Produce, inspect and retain the candidate
46	
47	Run `workflow STATE --root PROJECT_ROOT` or `pixl_workflow`. Resolve only the task's actual blockers. Sample work can investigate a proposed contract; production/delivery cannot treat that proposal as confirmed. Use the [production procedure](production.md) for authorized real tool execution. Missing tools leave the plan and local work useful; they do not supply a generated asset.
48	
49	Retrieve the actual candidate and store it under a new project-owned path. Record X with its byte hash, matching contract/kind, and `of` pointing to F. Nominate it through T.ca. Preserve older candidates when revising. Run applicable measurements, visually inspect the actual file/reference comparison, and execute required engine checks when available. Record an unavailable engine check as unavailable, not a pass or an artistic failure.
50	
51	For a saved raster candidate, use the [candidate inspection operation](inspection.md) to prepare exact native/enlarged views and retain an explicitly supplied review. It resolves the current plan and publishes the observation report with the required E/V bindings. The host still needs to view the actual images; preparation alone is unperformed review.
52	
53	For evidence outside that operation, retain the actual observation file and create E with its hash, timestamp, outcome, mode and full semantic bindings for both X and Q. Those bindings include the plan, contract, linked choices and sources. Then add V naming the task/candidate/criterion, reviewer, status, reason and E references; retain it in T.vr. `workflow` shows any absent verdict as unperformed. A local size/palette measurement cannot satisfy a Q requiring visual or live evidence.
54	
55	An unavailable V has `ev=[]` and a concrete reason. For example, a target project is absent, so its import behavior remains unknown. A failed V retains what was actually wrong. A current passing V is only the result for its exact candidate and criterion. Generic encoding cannot determine whether a claimed visual review truly occurred; the acting agent must inspect before making that claim.
56	
57	## Revise, finish or leave a resumable boundary
58	
59	- If a candidate fails, keep X/E/V, create the revised X and nominate it. Evaluate the new candidate against the saved criteria; it cannot borrow old bindings.
60	- If correcting a verdict, supersede the old V with `ob=true` and add a new V. Do not rewrite its previous outcome or reviewer. Supersede E only when its own observation is invalidated or replaced.
61	- If the plan, relevant choice or contract changes, preserve the change rationale/sources, reopen affected completed work, and supersede stale E/V. Commit the changed plan before publishing new evaluation. Do not merely recompute old receipt hashes.
62	- After all saved criteria pass, use `task-complete STORE TASK CANDIDATE... --expect HASH --root ROOT` or `pixl_task_complete` to nominate the explicit accepted candidates and finish the task. It validates existing acceptance, preserves every failed candidate/verdict, and publishes the legal state transitions; it does not supply a missing review. Read `workflow` afterward to confirm the durable result. [Operation contract](../../../resources/spec/task-completion.md).
63	- Mark T done only when all its nominated outputs satisfy every declared criterion and all prerequisite tasks are done. A mechanically valid but visually rejected sample stays unfinished. Deliver useful files while keeping an unavailable engine requirement explicit; do not label them fully accepted for that destination.
64	- Commit state and leave a handoff with the next task or unresolved requirement. A cold session starts with `workflow` and the focused `context`, inspecting retained observations before repeating work.
65	
66	This operation ends with either a representative sample accepted against its actual requirements, or a concrete retained boundary: missing choice, failed candidate, unavailable inspection, or next proof. Explain that useful outcome plainly; keep hashes, record IDs and mechanical details in evidence unless they clarify a conflict.
67	
68	If the next dependent step needs a consequential user choice, the final response must contain the useful progress saved, a direct concise question for the smallest set of necessary answers, and what those answers unlock. Address that question to the caller: a list of decisions needed or next steps once answered does not itself ask for the choice. Carry a still-unanswered question into that final response even when it was asked earlier or saved in the handoff. Present genuine alternatives when helpful and keep suggested trials labeled as proposals. Reference dimensions remain observations until adopted for this project. Continue authorized work that is independent of the answer. When the necessary choices are already supplied, use them and report the next operation under the existing authorization.
69	
70	## Check what an answer enables
71	
72	Name the next operation, its task and phase before claiming what an answer
73	unlocks. Read `workflow STATE --root ROOT` and
74	`context STATE TASK --view authoring --root ROOT` (or `pixl_workflow` and
75	`pixl_context` with that task as `focus` and `view="authoring"`). Keep the state
76	identity with this check. The workflow describes the saved plan, not every
77	possible future contract.
78	
79	Trace each planned output through **T.op → F.ct → C.ch → I**, reading the linked
80	choices' actual status, value, source and scope. When an output has no contract,
81	its current blockers cannot enumerate the choices a future contract would link.
82	Identify the intended contract and its links, or mark that future operation
83	conditional until they are selected. Inspect relevant `other_intake` entries;
84	unlinked choices are not automatically irrelevant. Do not drop applicable choice
85	links to make a readiness check pass.
86	
87	For production/delivery activation, account for completed task prerequisites,
88	concrete raster contracts, confirmation of every choice in those output
89	contracts, and the task's evidence-backed adoption decision. Check passing method
90	proofs when the task links knowledge, and baseline/destination gates when its
91	family plan declares them. Retrieve complete context when the authoring view
92	omits proof receipts. Read the source and proof scope of an adoption decision;
93	its existence does not confirm linked choices or establish its relevance to the
94	proposed work. Report only applicable missing prerequisites, not every possible
95	future gate or every intake choice in the project.
96	
97	In the saved decision table, project **only the supplied answer**: the exact
98	choice/contract change it supports, its authority and scope, the operation that
99	becomes available, and the prerequisites that remain. Keep other statuses and
100	scope unchanged. Drafting a contract, activating a production task and accepting
101	its artwork are different outcomes. A future projection is conditional reasoning,
102	not a fresh readiness result; after authorized changes are actually saved, rerun
103	workflow before claiming current readiness. Provider availability and required
104	visual/engine acceptance remain separate.
105	
106	### Write the current effect before the return
107	
108	Use this worksheet inside the new continuation note for each consequential answer
109	effect or claimed blocker. Shared prerequisite rows may be referenced rather than
110	repeated. It is a reasoning aid, not new PIXL syntax or proof of a correct review.
111	
112	```text
113	Current operation and answer effects
114	State/plan identity:
115	Operation and phase:
116	Question (or "no owner answer needed for this operation"):
117	Assume only this answer:
118	
119	Prerequisite or permitted alternative | Source + locator | Current status | After only this answer | Still required
120	
121	Current effect sentence:
122	Remaining prerequisites:
123	Authorized default/alternative (or none established):
124	Current carriers: note section; authored result field/JSON pointer; final wording
125	Prior instruction superseded: note/section + reason (when applicable)
126	```
127	
128	1. Fill the rows from the actual source and prerequisite trace above. Keep every
129	   unasked choice unchanged. Preserve source-defined alternatives: an allowed
130	   default and an owner-supplied value are alternative routes, not two mandatory
131	   inputs. An unknown future contract remains conditional.
132	2. Write the effect sentence from the completed rows. If anything needed for the
133	   claimed operation remains, name the narrower step available and the remaining
134	   requirements; do not say the answer clears the operation's gates. Do not treat
135	   an answer as completion of a prerequisite whose required work or evidence
136	   remains missing, or as confirmation of an unasked choice.
137	3. Make the current operation/condition section self-contained: carry every
138	   instruction governing that operation, including permitted alternatives.
139	   Old operational notes remain history/evidence, not parallel current
140	   instructions, even when linked by section. Cite unchanged sources and facts
141	   without duplicating history. Correct prior agent interpretations explicitly;
142	   the new note cannot supersede owner requirements or source criteria.
143	4. Build authored `question`, `necessary_for`, `unlocks`, `next` and `blocked_on`
144	   fields from these fresh checked statements, preserving their conditions and
145	   alternatives. Do not initialize their meaning from an old result's fields.
146	   Keep runtime-derived continuation unchanged; put authored explanation beside it.
147	5. For a saved JSON result, perform the [literal handoff review](handoff-review.md):
148	   inventory the whole question collection and whole authored next-operation
149	   subtree, review every listed value and bind the complete current instruction
150	   excerpts. Start with `python -B -I KIT/scripts/check_handoff.py RESULT --root ROOT --scope /remaining_questions --scope /next_action`, using the actual field names.
151	   Reopen the saved fields and current text after the coverage check and compare
152	   their meaning with the sources. Coverage is not semantic acceptance. Use the
153	   source-checked effect, with remaining requirements, in the final response.
154	
155	Use this check to ask only for information needed by the immediate dependent
156	operation. Existing source-backed decisions and authorization still apply; later
157	production requirements do not block an independently useful sample or local
158	plan. Keep the detailed trace in the note and return the useful next action and
159	its material remaining dependencies plainly.
160	
161	## Cold intake handoff
162	
163	1. Read the complete production profile and this procedure. Start with the saved
164	   workflow and focused context, then inspect the sources behind claimed blockers.
165	   Recover owner decisions and authorization separately from the predecessor's
166	   proposals, visual judgments and measurements. A diagnostic finding remains
167	   scoped to its tested artifact; it does not decide the owner's aesthetic or
168	   establish a requirement for a newly authored asset. Preserve earlier reports
169	   and identify overbroad inferences in the continuation.
170	
171	2. Save the [current-effect worksheet](#write-the-current-effect-before-the-return)
172	   in a new continuation note. Include observed/proposed choices with their real
173	   authority, source and scope; unasked rows keep their status. A diagnostic can
174	   support a recommendation without deciding for the owner. Keep the current
175	   operation section self-contained and continue independent useful work.
176	
177	3. Apply [the operation-effect check](#check-what-an-answer-enables) to the
178	   next local operation and any later operation the handoff claims to unlock.
179	   Trace the proposed contract's linked choices even when that contract is not
180	   yet saved. Keep its remaining phase/adoption dependencies explicit; preserve
181	   existing authorization and continue independent sample or planning work.
182	
183	4. Use the checked note to finish with saved progress, a direct concise question
184	   addressed to the caller, and the exact local operation its answer unlocks.
185	   A decision list or a statement that the owner should choose does not ask the
186	   question. If the necessary choices are already supplied, use them and state
187	   the next operation without asking again. Keep supporting diagnostics in the
188	   note; carry their scope and authority into any claim repeated in the response.
189	
190	When the representative sample is accepted and the assignment continues across a family, enter the [family and delivery operation](family-delivery.md). It records the exact nominated sample as the baseline, saves member and destination plans, and declares collective continuity before batch results. Replaced/rejected samples and unknown provider attempts must be reconciled before dependent production; an old artifact's existence is not baseline eligibility.

"""Run the copied kit's read-only handoff coverage utility."""

import runpy
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def main():
    # -I ignores PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE. Protect the read-only kit even when
    # callers omit -B; direct execution does not cache this launcher itself.
    sys.dont_write_bytecode = True
    runtime = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "runtime"
    if sys.version_info < (3, 11):  # noqa: UP036 - Copied launchers must reject old Python before runtime imports.
        print("PIXL requires Python 3.11 or newer.", file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(2)
    if not (runtime / "pixl/handoff_review.py").is_file():
        print("PIXL handoff review runtime is missing. Copy or reinstall the complete kit.", file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(2)
    sys.path.insert(0, str(runtime))
    runpy.run_module("pixl.handoff_review", run_name="__main__", alter_sys=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

38	do not narrow the scope to hide an unreviewed claim.

40	`-B` avoids creating Python import caches in the read-only kit; `-I` isolates the
41	interpreter from ambient Python configuration. Use these flags for this helper and
42	other Python reads of an assigned read-only kit. No global settings need changing.
43	The helper reads only by default. `--out` exclusively creates one fresh confined

77	}

def _activation_blockers(doc, task_id, scope, bound):
    from . import families

    task = doc.records[task_id].fields
    reasons = []
    for dependency in task["dp"]:
        state = doc.records[dependency.id].fields["st"].value
        if state != "done":
            reasons.append(f"task_prerequisite: {dependency.id} is {state}; it must be done")
    for reference in task["op"]:
        output = doc.records[reference.id].fields
        if output["kd"].value not in NONRASTER and "ct" not in output:
            reasons.append(f"output_contract: {reference.id} needs a concrete raster contract")
    choice_ids = sorted(_output_choices(doc, task))
    for choice_id in choice_ids:
        choice = doc.records[choice_id].fields
        state = choice["st"].value
        if state in {"unresolved", "conflict"}:
            reasons.append(
                f"choice_{state}: {choice_id} ({choice['ky']}) is {state}; resolve it before active work"
            )
    if task["ph"].value in ADOPTION_PHASES:
        if not task["dc"]:
            reasons.append(f"task_decision: {task_id} needs an evidence-backed adoption decision")
        for reference in task["kn"]:
            method = doc.records[reference.id].fields
            if not scope(reference.id) <= bound(method.get("pc", []), passing=True):
                reasons.append(f"method_poc: {reference.id} needs current passing method proof")
        for choice_id in choice_ids:
            choice = doc.records[choice_id].fields
            if choice["st"].value in {"observed", "proposed"}:
                reasons.append(f"choice_unconfirmed: {choice_id} ({choice['ky']}) must be confirmed")
    reasons.extend(families.blockers(doc, task_id))
    return reasons

def prepare(
    folder: PathInput,
    expected: str,
    job_id: str,
    task_id: str,
    outputs: object,
    provider: str,
    tool: str,
    arguments: JsonObject,
    schema: JsonObject,
    discovery: JsonObject,
    authorization: JsonObject,
    root: PathInput | None = None,
) -> JobMutationResult:
    folder, root, doc = _load(folder, expected, root)
    _require(
        job_id not in doc.records, "job_exists", "use a new job ID for a new attempt"
    )
    context = _context(doc, task_id, outputs)
    reasons = _blockers(doc, task_id, root)
    _require(not reasons, "job_blocked", "; ".join(reasons))
    _pending(doc, task_id, outputs, root=root)
    request = platform.prepare_discovered(
        provider, tool, arguments, schema, discovery, authorization
    )
    journal = job_history.new(job_id, request, context)
    return _save(folder, root, doc, journal, expected)

    if task["ph"].value in ADOPTION_PHASES:

F1-F5. All five are correct. This note records the old-to-new correction for each and otherwise
directs readers to the b note, which remains the current full continuation. This is still a
**handoff-only increment**: no request packet, criteria v2, fixture, harness, generation, provider,

`5f49e8f3...`) + `pixl-kit/bundle-manifest.json` itself + `pixl-kit/requirements.txt`, the only file
listed under the manifest's `generated_files` (`sha256 9cc16454cea28c8f5e5b6dbd150434f0c3259f698a6fd65086e275760d5891f3`).
`pixl_readiness` `files_checked 260` = 259 `files` entries + the generated `requirements.txt`. The
counts in the b note (261 / 259 / 260) were right; the attribution of the 261st file was wrong. The b
note's new-file table (lines 97-105) is unaffected: `resources/pixl/handoff_review.py` is both
manifest-listed and new relative to the revision 14 snapshot.

(`fbcd6091...`, `coverage_complete`), bound to the same result hash `7d80d6f9...`. New: the b result and

revision 15 inventory scopes were `/questions`, `/next`, `/limitations`; `/status` had no review row

unchanged.

fails with "scope and claim pointers must be JSON Pointers". This is not a kit fault: it succeeds
